fighter.name: Fighter

skills.text: Choose 2: Acrobatics, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, Survival

fighter.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Chain hauberk, longsword, shield, light crossbow and 20 bolts, a delver's pack; or (B) 135 gc.

description.p: Mail from neck to knee over a padded coat. Strength 13.
The knight's blade: long enough to keep death an arm away.
Wood or metal on the arm: +2 Defense.
A light crossbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 80/320), Loading, Two-Handed.
Ammunition for crossbows.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.

text.p: Fighters stand between the party and what comes out of the dark. They wear the heaviest armour, use every weapon, and keep going when others fall.

Choose a way of fighting: Shieldwall (+1 Defense with a shield), Bladework (+2 to damage with a one-handed weapon and nothing in the other hand), Marksman (+2 to ranged attack rolls) or Brute (reroll 1s and 2s on the damage dice of a two-handed weapon, once).
Once per safe rest, as a bonus action, you regain 1d10 + your Fighter level Health.
Once per safe rest, on your turn, you take one more action.
You score a critical hit on a 19 or 20. Your first point of Dread each fight is ignored.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
When you take the Attack action you attack twice.
When a creature within 5 feet of you hits an ally, you may use your reaction to make one weapon attack against it.
You have advantage on saves against being frightened, and a safe rest lowers your Dread by 2, not 1.
Once per safe rest, reroll a saving throw you failed; you must use the new roll.
Allies within 10 feet of you who can see you add 1 to their saves. Second Breath heals 2d10 + your level.

cleric.name: Cleric

armor.text: Light and medium armour and shields

skills.text: Choose 2: History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion

cleric.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Scale hauberk, mace, shield, holy symbol, healer's satchel, a delver's pack; or (B) 85 gc.

description.p: Overlapping plates of steel on a leather coat.
A mace.
Wood or metal on the arm: +2 Defense.
A cleric's or paladin's focus: an amulet, a reliquary, a sigil painted on a shield.
Bandages, salves and splints for ten uses. An action and a use steadies a dying creature without a check, or lets a creature spend one Recovery Die outside a rest.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.

text.p: Clerics carry a light that is not a lantern's. They mend the wounded, steady the afraid, and turn back the dead that should not walk.

You cast cleric spells with Wisdom: spell save DC 8 + your proficiency + Wisdom; spell attack your proficiency + Wisdom. You know every cleric spell of a circle you can cast; prepare a number of them equal to your Wisdom modifier + your level after a safe rest.
Your holy symbol is a light: as a bonus action it sheds bright light 20 feet and dim 20 beyond until you douse it, burning no oil.
Once per safe rest (twice from 6th level), as an action, present your symbol: each undead within 30 feet that can see it makes a Wisdom save against your spell DC or flees for a minute.
As an action, a companion within 30 feet loses 1 Dread. Once per safe rest; twice from 6th level.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
When an undead of low power (the GM says) fails its save against Turn the Dead, it is destroyed.
Within your Lantern of Faith's bright light, companions have advantage on saves against being frightened.
Once on each of your turns, a weapon hit or cantrip deals 1d8 radiant damage more.
Once per week, call on your faith for something only a god could do; the GM decides how it is answered.

wizard.name: Wizard

weapons.text: Daggers, quarterstaffs, slings and light crossbows

skills.text: Choose 2: Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Religion

wizard.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Quarterstaff, dagger, spellbook, arcane focus, a scholar's pack; or (B) 70 gc.

description.p: A quarterstaff. Properties: Versatile (1d8).
A long knife, the last weapon anyone gives up.
A wizard's book of spells: 100 vellum pages, a lock, and the smell of old candle smoke.
A wizard's or bard's focus: a wand, a crystal, a worn instrument.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
Burns for six turns: dim light 5 feet. Enough to read by, not enough to fight by.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.

text.p: Wizards read the dark, and sometimes it reads back. They are fragile, and the most dangerous people in any room.

You cast wizard spells with Intelligence: spell save DC 8 + your proficiency + Intelligence; spell attack your proficiency + Intelligence. Your spellbook holds six 1st-circle spells and you learn two more each level; prepare Intelligence modifier + level of them after a safe rest.
Once per safe rest, after a short rest of an exploration turn, you regain spell slots whose circles add up to half your level (rounded up), none higher than 5th.
Choose Arcana, History or Religion: your proficiency bonus doubles for it.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
When you cast a spell that makes several creatures save, choose up to your Intelligence modifier of them: they succeed automatically and take no damage.
Once per safe rest, when a creature you can see would gain Dread from magic, it does not.
Choose a 1st-circle spell you know: you can cast it without a slot.
You learn Unweave and always have it prepared; once per safe rest you cast it without a slot.

thief.name: Thief

weapons.text: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, rapiers and shortswords

skills.text: Choose 4: Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth

thief.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Leather jerkin, shortsword, two daggers, shortbow and 20 arrows, thieves' tools, a delver's pack; or (B) 85 gc.

description.p: Boiled and oiled leather over the chest and shoulders.
A shortsword. Properties: Finesse, Light.
A long knife, the last weapon anyone gives up.
A shortbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 80/320), Two-Handed.
Ammunition for bows.
Picks, a small file, a mirror on a stick and a pair of narrow pliers. Needed to pick locks and disarm traps.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.

text.p: Thieves go first into the dark and come back with what was in it. Locks, traps and unwary throats are their trade.

Once per turn, a hit with a finesse or ranged weapon deals 1d6 more damage when you have advantage, or when an ally stands within 5 feet of your target. The bonus grows by 1d6 at every odd level (2d6 at 3rd, 3d6 at 5th, and so on).
You speak the thieves' cant, and you are proficient with thieves' tools: double your proficiency bonus for them.
As a bonus action on your turn: Dash, Disengage or Hide.
You can pick a lock, disarm a trap or use a healer's satchel as a bonus action.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
When an attacker you can see hits you, use your reaction to halve the damage.
When a spell or trap lets you make a Dexterity save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.
In dim light or darkness you have advantage on Stealth, and a creature that does not see you does not gain advantage against you.
Once per safe rest, turn a miss into a hit, or a failed check into a 20.

paladin.name: Paladin

skills.text: Choose 2: Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion

paladin.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Chain hauberk, longsword, shield, two spears, holy symbol, a delver's pack; or (B) 115 gc.

description.p: Mail from neck to knee over a padded coat. Strength 13.
The knight's blade: long enough to keep death an arm away.
Wood or metal on the arm: +2 Defense.
A spear. Properties: Thrown (Range 20/60), Versatile (1d8).
A cleric's or paladin's focus: an amulet, a reliquary, a sigil painted on a shield.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.

text.p: Paladins have sworn to stand against the dark, and their oath stands with them: it heals by their hands, and burns in their blade.
You have a pool of healing equal to five times your Paladin level, refilled by a safe rest. As an action, touch a creature and give it Health from the pool, or spend 5 to end a disease or poison.
As an action, you know where undead and fiends are within 60 feet, until the end of your next turn. Once per safe rest, plus your Charisma modifier.
From 2nd level you cast paladin spells with Charisma; slots as a half-caster (Kraken counts them).
When you hit with a melee weapon, spend a spell slot: 2d8 radiant damage more, +1d8 per circle above the first, +1d8 against undead or fiends.
You and companions within 10 feet of you cannot be frightened while you are conscious.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
When you take the Attack action you attack twice.
You and companions within 10 feet add your Charisma modifier (at least 1) to their saving throws while you are conscious.
Every melee weapon hit you make deals 1d8 radiant damage more.

ranger.name: Ranger

armor.text: Light and medium armour and shields

skills.text: Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival

ranger.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Hide coat, two shortswords, longbow and 40 arrows, a delver's pack; or (B) 90 gc.

description.p: Thick furs and hides, the hunter's armour.
A shortsword. Properties: Finesse, Light.
A longbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 150/600), Heavy, Two-Handed.
Ammunition for bows.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.

text.p: Rangers know the wild places between the towns and the ruins, and what hunts there. They track it, and they hunt it back.
You and companions travelling with you cannot be lost by anything but magic, and you always know which way is north and how far you have come. Foraging finds food for two more people.
Choose beasts, the undead, or the folk of the deep (goblins and their kin): advantage to track them and recall what you know of them, and +2 damage against them.
From 2nd level you cast ranger spells with Wisdom; slots as a half-caster.
Archer (+2 to ranged attack rolls) or Twin Blades (add your ability modifier to the off-hand attack's damage).
Once per turn, a weapon hit on a creature you have marked with Hunter's Quarry deals 1d8 more damage.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
When you take the Attack action you attack twice.
You see in dim light as if it were bright, and in darkness 30 feet as if it were dim.
Hiding is a bonus action for you, and you stay hidden after a missed attack.

bard.name: Bard

weapons.text: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers and shortswords

bard.startingequipment: Choose A or B: (A) Leather jerkin, rapier, dagger, a worn instrument (arcane focus), a delver's pack; or (B) 55 gc.

description.p: Boiled and oiled leather over the chest and shoulders.
A rapier. Properties: Finesse.
A long knife, the last weapon anyone gives up.
A wizard's or bard's focus: a wand, a crystal, a worn instrument.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).

A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.

text.p: Bards are lorekeepers: they remember the old songs, the names of the dead, and where the stairs go. Their stories keep the dark at bay.
You cast bard spells with Charisma: spell save DC 8 + your proficiency + Charisma. You know four spells and learn one more each level.

Three times per safe rest (more with Charisma: your modifier, at least 3), when a companion who can hear you rolls a d20, add 1d4 to it after seeing the roll but before the outcome is told. The die is 1d6 at 5th level and 1d8 at 9th.
During a safe rest, every companion who listens regains 1 more Health per Recovery Die spent, and loses 1 Dread more.
Add half your proficiency bonus to checks you are not proficient in.
Choose two skills you are proficient in: double your proficiency bonus for them. Two more at 10th level.
Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
As an action, until the end of your next turn, companions who can hear you have advantage on saves against being frightened and ignore new Dread.
Learn two spells from any class's list; they are bard spells for you.

human.name: Human
human.classes: Fighter, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Paladin, Ranger, Bard

text.p: The most numerous folk, and the most stubborn. Humans build towns on the bones of older towns and swear this time will be different.
A human may take any class.
Once per safe rest, when you would gain Dread, ignore one point of it.
You are proficient in one skill of your choice.

elf.name: Elf
elf.classes: Fighter, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Ranger, Bard

text.p: Elves live long and remember longer. They were old when the first towers fell, and they have watched the dark rise before.

In faint light you make out shapes and find your way as well as in daylight, 60 feet around you; you cannot read fine writing or see detail at a distance. In total darkness you see nothing, like anyone.
You are proficient in Perception.
Advantage on checks to recall the history of a place or a thing older than a human lifetime.

halfelf.name: Half-Elf
halfelf.classes: Fighter, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Ranger, Bard

text.p: Born of two peoples and at home in neither, half-elves make their own way, and are often very good at it.
As an elf's, to 30 feet.
You are proficient in two skills of your choice.
Dwarves dug the first deep halls, and lost most of them. They are hard, slow to trust, and slower to forgive.
As an elf's, to 60 feet.
+1 Health at each level. Advantage on saves against poison.
Advantage on checks about stonework: its age, who made it, where it is weak, and where a passage leads.
Small, curious and impossible to bore, gnomes take apart locks, clocks and spells to see how they work, and usually put them back together.
As an elf's, to 60 feet.
Advantage on checks to understand, open or disable a mechanism: a lock, a trap, a clockwork.
You can move through the space of a creature larger than you.

gravedigger.name: Grave Digger

text.p: You buried the dead of a town that had too many. You know the old rites, and what a disturbed grave looks like.

gravedigger.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Shovel, Holy Symbol, 10 gc; or (B) 20 gc. A shovel, a holy symbol of the dead, 10 gc

description.p: For graves, latrines, and digging out what the earth took back.
A cleric's or paladin's focus: an amulet, a reliquary, a sigil painted on a shield.

lamplighter.name: Lamplighter

text.p: You kept the street lamps of a city burning through the long nights. You know how long a flame lasts, and what moves when it goes out.

lamplighter.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Lantern, Hooded, 2 Oil, Flask, 10 gc; or (B) 20 gc. A hooded lantern, two flasks of oil, 10 gc

description.p: Burns a flask of oil for 24 turns (four hours): bright light 30 feet, dim 30 beyond. Hooded, it gives only dim light 5 feet.
Fuel for a lantern (24 turns). Thrown and set alight, it burns a creature for 1d4 fire a turn for two turns.

deserter.name: Deserter

text.p: You fled a war you did not believe in, and they are still looking for you.

deserter.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Dagger, 5 gc; or (B) 10 gc. A worn sword-belt, a forged pass, 5 gc

description.p: A long knife, the last weapon anyone gives up.

acolyteoftheash.name: Acolyte of the Ash

text.p: You served a temple that keeps vigil fires against the dark. Its priests will give you a meal and a bed, and ask questions.

acolyteoftheash.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Holy Symbol, 10 gc; or (B) 15 gc. A holy symbol, prayer beads, incense, 10 gc

description.p: A cleric's or paladin's focus: an amulet, a reliquary, a sigil painted on a shield.

smuggler.name: Smuggler

text.p: You moved what was not allowed across borders that were not watched. You know who to pay, and how much.

smuggler.equipment: 15 gc. A coat with hidden pockets, 15 gc

hedgescholar.name: Hedge Scholar

text.p: You learned from books nobody else wanted, in libraries nobody else visited.

hedgescholar.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Ink and Quill, 10 gc; or (B) 15 gc. Ink, a quill, a book of half-remembered lore, 10 gc

description.p: A small bottle of ink and a quill: enough for a map, a letter, or a copied page.

hunter.name: Hunter

text.p: You fed your family from the forest's edge, and learned which tracks to follow and which to run from.

hunter.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Hunting Trap, Dagger, 10 gc; or (B) 20 gc. A hunting trap, a skinning knife, 10 gc

description.p: Iron jaws on a chain. A creature that steps in makes a Dexterity save (DC 13) or takes 1d4 piercing damage and is held until it or someone else breaks free (Strength, DC 13).
A long knife, the last weapon anyone gives up.

streetrat.name: Street Rat

text.p: You grew up on the streets and the rooftops, fed by quick hands and quicker feet.

streetrat.equipment: Choose A or B: (A) Lucky Charm, 5 gc; or (B) 10 gc. A map of a city's back ways, a lucky charm, 5 gc

description.p: A rabbit's foot, a saint's bone, a coin with a hole in it. Once per safe rest, when you gain Dread, you may ignore one point of it.

A small object you touch sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond, for an hour or until you kindle another. The light is cold; it burns nothing and no wind puts it out. In the Darkness, it is the first spell every apprentice learns and the last one they forget.

A whip of sparks cracks at a creature you can see. Make a ranged spell attack: on a hit, 1d10 fire damage, and a flammable object it strikes catches. The damage grows by 1d10 at 5th level and again at 11th.

Your hand carries the cold of a burial vault. Make a melee spell attack: on a hit, 1d8 necrotic damage, and the target cannot regain Health until the start of your next turn. More dice at 5th and 11th level.
A mote of holy fire falls on a creature you can see. It makes a Dexterity save or takes 1d8 radiant damage; cover does not help it. More dice at 5th and 11th level.
You find the thing a creature fears to hear. It makes a Wisdom save or takes 1d6 psychic damage and has disadvantage on its next attack. More dice at 5th and 11th level.
A creature you touch carries a small certainty: once before the spell ends it adds 1d4 to an ability check of its choice.
One break or tear in an object you touch closes: a broken chain link, a torn cloak, a cracked lamp. Magic items are beyond it.
An invisible hand does simple work within range: opens an unlocked door, carries 10 pounds, pulls a lever. It cannot attack.
You whisper to a creature you can see; only it hears, and it may whisper back. Stone a foot thick, or metal, stops it.
Three darts of force fly at creatures of your choice and never miss: each deals 1d4 + 1 force damage. A higher-circle casting adds a dart per circle above the first.
A creature you touch regains 1d8 + your spellcasting modifier Health. Each circle above the first heals 1d8 more. It cannot mend the dead.
A word of comfort carries across the fight: a creature you can see regains 1d4 + your spellcasting modifier Health. Each circle above the first heals 1d4 more.
A shimmer of faith stands between a creature you choose and harm: +2 Defense while the spell lasts.
Up to three creatures of your choice add 1d4 to their attack rolls and saving throws while it lasts.
Fire spreads from your fingers in a fan. Each creature in a 15-foot cone makes a Dexterity save: 3d6 fire damage, half on a success. Each circle above the first adds 1d6.
A heavy drowsiness rolls over a creature. It makes a Wisdom save or falls asleep for a minute, until it takes damage or someone shakes it awake. Creatures that do not sleep are not affected.

You show a creature the dark it came from. It makes a Wisdom save or is frightened of you for a minute (it repeats the save at the end of each of its turns). A player character who fails also gains 1 Dread.
An unseen barrier of will snaps into place: +5 Defense until your next turn, including against the attack that triggered it.

A peal of thunder rolls out from you. Each creature in a 15-foot cube makes a Constitution save: 2d8 thunder damage and pushed 10 feet away, or half damage and not pushed on a success. Heard 300 feet away.
Up to five falling creatures drift down at 60 feet a round and land unhurt.
You mark a creature as your quarry: your weapon hits on it deal 1d6 more damage, and you have advantage to track or spot it.
A steady glow surrounds you: bright light 30 feet and dim 30 beyond, for an hour. While it lasts, you and companions within its bright light ignore the first point of Dread you would each gain.
You sense magic within 30 feet, and the hidden: secret doors, concealed traps and invisible creatures show as a faint outline to you. Stone a foot thick blocks it.
A beam of white fire. Make a ranged spell attack: on a hit, 4d6 fire damage. Each circle above the second adds 1d6.
A humanoid you can see makes a Wisdom save or is held fast, unable to move or act, for a minute (it repeats the save at the end of each turn).
Your weapon burns with pale silver: its hits deal 2d6 radiant damage more, and the undead and fiends you strike shed dim light 5 feet and cannot hide.
Magical darkness fills a 15-foot sphere. No light but magic of the third circle or higher shows anything inside it; creatures there are unseen. Every adventurer in it gains 1 Dread the first time.
You end one disease or one condition on a creature you touch: blinded, deafened, paralyzed or poisoned. Or you take 1 Dread from it.
You become mist and reform up to 30 feet away in a space you can see.
Up to five creatures of your choice regain 1d8 + your spellcasting modifier Health each.
A bead of flame bursts at a point you choose. Each creature in a 20-foot sphere makes a Dexterity save: 8d6 fire damage, half on a success. Fire spreads around corners and lights what will burn.
A spear of lightning 100 feet long and 5 feet wide. Each creature in it makes a Dexterity save: 8d6 lightning damage, half on a success.
Up to six creatures you can see lose 2 Dread each and cannot gain Dread for the next hour. A creature that is frightened is no longer.
You touch a creature that died within the last minute and call it back: it returns to life with 1 Health and 2 Dread. It cannot return if it was not willing, or if its body was destroyed.

unweave.name: Unweave
unweave.castingtime: Reaction, when a creature you can see casts a spell

description.p: You pull the threads of a spell apart as it is cast. A spell of the third circle or lower fails; a higher one fails if you succeed on an ability check with your spellcasting ability (DC 10 + its circle).
Shining spirits circle you. A foe that starts its turn within 15 feet of you, or enters the area, makes a Wisdom save: 3d8 radiant damage, half on a success. The area is bright light.
A long knife, the last weapon anyone gives up.
A club. Properties: Light.
A heavy length of oak bound in iron at one end.
A handaxe. Properties: Light, Thrown (Range 20/60).
A mace.
A spear. Properties: Thrown (Range 20/60), Versatile (1d8).
A quarterstaff. Properties: Versatile (1d8).
A sickle. Properties: Light.
A sling. Properties: Ammunition (Range 30/120).
A shortbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 80/320), Two-Handed.
A light crossbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 80/320), Loading, Two-Handed.
A shortsword. Properties: Finesse, Light.
The knight's blade: long enough to keep death an arm away.
A rapier. Properties: Finesse.
A battleaxe. Properties: Versatile (1d10).
A warhammer. Properties: Versatile (1d10).
A flail.
A morningstar.
A greatsword. Properties: Heavy, Two-Handed.
A greataxe. Properties: Heavy, Two-Handed.
A halberd. Properties: Heavy, Reach, Two-Handed.
A longbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 150/600), Heavy, Two-Handed.
A hand crossbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 30/120), Light, Loading.
A heavy crossbow. Properties: Ammunition (Range 100/400), Heavy, Loading, Two-Handed.
Layers of stitched cloth. Better than nothing, and warm.
Boiled and oiled leather over the chest and shoulders.
Leather sewn with iron rings, quiet enough for thieves.
Thick furs and hides, the hunter's armour.
A shirt of interlocking rings under a tunic.
Overlapping plates of steel on a leather coat.
A fitted steel breast and back.
Heavy leather with iron rings sewn close.
Mail from neck to knee over a padded coat. Strength 13.
Shaped steel plates over every part of the body. Strength 15.
Wood or metal on the arm: +2 Defense.
A torch burns for six exploration turns (an hour). It sheds bright light 20 feet and dim light 20 feet beyond. Lit, it shows everyone where you are.
Burns a flask of oil for 24 turns (four hours): bright light 30 feet, dim 30 beyond. Hooded, it gives only dim light 5 feet.
Burns a flask of oil for 24 turns: a 60-foot cone of bright light and 60 feet of dim beyond. The cone must point somewhere.
Fuel for a lantern (24 turns). Thrown and set alight, it burns a creature for 1d4 fire a turn for two turns.
Burns for six turns: dim light 5 feet. Enough to read by, not enough to fight by.
Flint, steel and tinder. Lighting a torch takes an action; in the wind or wet, a Dexterity check (DC 12).
Strong enough for two climbers. A Strength check (DC 18) breaks it.
An iron hook for a rope's end.
Advantage on Strength checks where leverage helps: a jammed door, a coffin lid.
For wedging doors shut, or open.
For marking the way back. Every dungeon has someone who forgot to.
For prodding what you would rather not step on.
Scattered over a 5-foot square: whoever enters stops and makes a Dexterity save (DC 15) or takes 1 piercing damage and moves at half speed until healed.
A safe rest needs one (or a bed).
Dried meat, hard bread, an onion. A safe rest needs food and water.
Holds a day's water.
Holds 30 pounds of gear.
Bandages, salves and splints for ten uses. An action and a use steadies a dying creature without a check, or lets a creature spend one Recovery Die outside a rest.
A cleric's or paladin's focus: an amulet, a reliquary, a sigil painted on a shield.
A wizard's or bard's focus: a wand, a crystal, a worn instrument.
A wizard's book of spells: 100 vellum pages, a lock, and the smell of old candle smoke.
Picks, a small file, a mirror on a stick and a pair of narrow pliers. Needed to pick locks and disarm traps.
For looking round corners, and at what you should not look at directly.
Iron cuffs. Escaping them: Dexterity (DC 18); breaking them: Strength (DC 20).
For graves, latrines, and digging out what the earth took back.
Iron jaws on a chain. A creature that steps in makes a Dexterity save (DC 13) or takes 1d4 piercing damage and is held until it or someone else breaks free (Strength, DC 13).
A small bottle of ink and a quill: enough for a map, a letter, or a copied page.
A rabbit's foot, a saint's bone, a coin with a hole in it. Once per safe rest, when you gain Dread, you may ignore one point of it.
Ammunition for bows.
Ammunition for crossbows.
Ammunition for slings.

text.p: Descending Darkness is a game of fragile people going into dangerous places, and some of them coming back.

The towns hold. Past their walls the old roads run into ruins, barrows and drowned halls, where the light of a torch is the whole world and the dark beyond it is listening. Your characters go there for gold, for answers, for someone who did not come home.
One player is the Game Master: they describe the world, play everyone who lives in it, and decide what the dice mean. The others each play an adventurer. Together you find out what happens.
This book is for everyone. The Game Master's Guide and the Bestiary are for the Game Master.

When the outcome is uncertain and something is at stake, roll a d20, add the ability modifier that fits (and your proficiency bonus if you are trained in what you are doing), and compare the total to the difficulty:
Meet or beat it and you succeed. Before you roll, the Game Master tells you what failing would cost: time, light, position, Health, or attention from something in the dark.
Advantage (something helps you): roll two d20 and keep the higher. Disadvantage: keep the lower. They cancel each other.
In Kraken, click any number on your sheet to roll it in front of the table; set the DC on the sheet first and the result says success or failure.
Six abilities describe every character: Strength, Dexterity, Constitution, Intelligence, Wisdom and Charisma. The modifier is the score minus 10, halved and rounded down.
Your proficiency bonus is +2 at levels 1 to 4, +3 at 5 to 8 and +4 at 9 and 10. Add it to checks with skills you are trained in, to saves your class knows, and to attacks with weapons you know.

list.li: 1. Choose a kin: human, elf, half-elf, dwarf or gnome. Your kin limits your class.
2. Choose a class: fighter, cleric, wizard, thief, paladin, ranger or bard.
3. Assign ability scores: put 17, 14, 14, 13, 12 and 8 where you like, then apply your kin's adjustments.
4. Choose a background (two skills) and your class's skills.
5. Take your class's starting gear, name your character, and say one thing they are afraid of.

text.p: Your Health at 1st level is your class's hit die at its highest plus your Constitution modifier. Each level after adds the die rolled (or its average, rounded up) plus your Constitution modifier.
In Kraken, the Characters window's Character Wizard does all of this: it knows your kin's adjustments and which classes your kin may take.
You gain experience for treasure brought back to safety, for dangers overcome, and for discoveries. The Game Master awards it at the end of a session.
Tenth level is the height of a mortal career. Beyond it lie stories, not levels.

p.i: The most numerous folk, and the most stubborn. Humans build towns on the bones of older towns and swear this time will be different.

text.p: Size Medium. Speed 30 feet. Abilities no adjustment. Classes Fighter, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Paladin, Ranger, Bard.
Any Path. A human may take any class.
Stubborn. Once per safe rest, when you would gain Dread, ignore one point of it.
Quick Study. You are proficient in one skill of your choice.

p.i: Elves live long and remember longer. They were old when the first towers fell, and they have watched the dark rise before.

text.p: Size Medium. Speed 30 feet. Abilities Dexterity +1, Constitution -1. Classes Fighter, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Ranger, Bard.

Dimsight. In faint light you make out shapes and find your way as well as in daylight, 60 feet around you; you cannot read fine writing or see detail at a distance. In total darkness you see nothing, like anyone.
Keen Senses. You are proficient in Perception.
Long Memory. Advantage on checks to recall the history of a place or a thing older than a human lifetime.

p.i: Born of two peoples and at home in neither, half-elves make their own way, and are often very good at it.

text.p: Size Medium. Speed 30 feet. Abilities no adjustment. Classes Fighter, Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Ranger, Bard.
Dimsight. As an elf's, to 30 feet.
Two Worlds. You are proficient in two skills of your choice.

p.i: Dwarves dug the first deep halls, and lost most of them. They are hard, slow to trust, and slower to forgive.

text.p: Size Medium. Speed 25 feet. Abilities Constitution +1, Charisma -1. Classes Fighter, Cleric, Thief.
Dimsight. As an elf's, to 60 feet.
Hardy. +1 Health at each level. Advantage on saves against poison.
Stonewise. Advantage on checks about stonework: its age, who made it, where it is weak, and where a passage leads.

p.i: Small, curious and impossible to bore, gnomes take apart locks, clocks and spells to see how they work, and usually put them back together.

text.p: Size Small. Speed 25 feet. Abilities Intelligence +1, Wisdom -1. Classes Cleric, Wizard, Thief, Bard.
Dimsight. As an elf's, to 60 feet.
Tinker's Eye. Advantage on checks to understand, open or disable a mechanism: a lock, a trap, a clockwork.
Small and Quick. You can move through the space of a creature larger than you.

p.i: Fighters stand between the party and what comes out of the dark. They wear the heaviest armour, use every weapon, and keep going when others fall.

text.p: Skills. Choose 2: Acrobatics, Athletics, History, Insight, Intimidation, Perception, Survival. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Chain hauberk, longsword, shield, light crossbow and 20 bolts, a delver's pack; or (B) 135 gc.

Hard Lessons (level 1). Choose a way of fighting: Shieldwall (+1 Defense with a shield), Bladework (+2 to damage with a one-handed weapon and nothing in the other hand), Marksman (+2 to ranged attack rolls) or Brute (reroll 1s and 2s on the damage dice of a two-handed weapon, once).
Second Breath (level 1). Once per safe rest, as a bonus action, you regain 1d10 + your Fighter level Health.
Press On (level 2). Once per safe rest, on your turn, you take one more action.
Battle-Scarred (level 3). You score a critical hit on a 19 or 20. Your first point of Dread each fight is ignored.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Extra Attack (level 5). When you take the Attack action you attack twice.
Hold the Line (level 6). When a creature within 5 feet of you hits an ally, you may use your reaction to make one weapon attack against it.
Iron Nerve (level 7). You have advantage on saves against being frightened, and a safe rest lowers your Dread by 2, not 1.
Indomitable (level 9). Once per safe rest, reroll a saving throw you failed; you must use the new roll.
Champion of the Lost (level 10). Allies within 10 feet of you who can see you add 1 to their saves. Second Breath heals 2d10 + your level.

p.i: Clerics carry a light that is not a lantern's. They mend the wounded, steady the afraid, and turn back the dead that should not walk.

tr.td: Light and medium armour and shields

text.p: Skills. Choose 2: History, Insight, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Scale hauberk, mace, shield, holy symbol, healer's satchel, a delver's pack; or (B) 85 gc.

Spellcasting (level 1). You cast cleric spells with Wisdom: spell save DC 8 + your proficiency + Wisdom; spell attack your proficiency + Wisdom. You know every cleric spell of a circle you can cast; prepare a number of them equal to your Wisdom modifier + your level after a safe rest.
Lantern of Faith (level 1). Your holy symbol is a light: as a bonus action it sheds bright light 20 feet and dim 20 beyond until you douse it, burning no oil.

Turn the Dead (level 2). Once per safe rest (twice from 6th level), as an action, present your symbol: each undead within 30 feet that can see it makes a Wisdom save against your spell DC or flees for a minute.
Steadying Word (level 2). As an action, a companion within 30 feet loses 1 Dread. Once per safe rest; twice from 6th level.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Burn the Dead (level 5). When an undead of low power (the GM says) fails its save against Turn the Dead, it is destroyed.
Sanctuary of Light (level 6). Within your Lantern of Faith's bright light, companions have advantage on saves against being frightened.
Blessed Strikes (level 8). Once on each of your turns, a weapon hit or cantrip deals 1d8 radiant damage more.
Miracle (level 10). Once per week, call on your faith for something only a god could do; the GM decides how it is answered.

p.i: Wizards read the dark, and sometimes it reads back. They are fragile, and the most dangerous people in any room.

tr.td: Daggers, quarterstaffs, slings and light crossbows

text.p: Skills. Choose 2: Arcana, History, Insight, Investigation, Medicine, Religion. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Quarterstaff, dagger, spellbook, arcane focus, a scholar's pack; or (B) 70 gc.

Spellcasting (level 1). You cast wizard spells with Intelligence: spell save DC 8 + your proficiency + Intelligence; spell attack your proficiency + Intelligence. Your spellbook holds six 1st-circle spells and you learn two more each level; prepare Intelligence modifier + level of them after a safe rest.
Quiet Study (level 1). Once per safe rest, after a short rest of an exploration turn, you regain spell slots whose circles add up to half your level (rounded up), none higher than 5th.
Lorekeeper (level 2). Choose Arcana, History or Religion: your proficiency bonus doubles for it.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Sculpted Spells (level 5). When you cast a spell that makes several creatures save, choose up to your Intelligence modifier of them: they succeed automatically and take no damage.
Words of Warding (level 6). Once per safe rest, when a creature you can see would gain Dread from magic, it does not.
Spell Mastery (level 9). Choose a 1st-circle spell you know: you can cast it without a slot.
Unweaving Hand (level 10). You learn Unweave and always have it prepared; once per safe rest you cast it without a slot.

p.i: Thieves go first into the dark and come back with what was in it. Locks, traps and unwary throats are their trade.

tr.td: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, rapiers and shortswords

text.p: Skills. Choose 4: Acrobatics, Athletics, Deception, Insight, Intimidation, Investigation, Perception, Performance, Persuasion, Sleight of Hand, Stealth. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Leather jerkin, shortsword, two daggers, shortbow and 20 arrows, thieves' tools, a delver's pack; or (B) 85 gc.

Sneak Strike (level 1). Once per turn, a hit with a finesse or ranged weapon deals 1d6 more damage when you have advantage, or when an ally stands within 5 feet of your target. The bonus grows by 1d6 at every odd level (2d6 at 3rd, 3d6 at 5th, and so on).
Cant and Craft (level 1). You speak the thieves' cant, and you are proficient with thieves' tools: double your proficiency bonus for them.
Slip Away (level 2). As a bonus action on your turn: Dash, Disengage or Hide.
Light Fingers (level 3). You can pick a lock, disarm a trap or use a healer's satchel as a bonus action.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Duck and Weave (level 5). When an attacker you can see hits you, use your reaction to halve the damage.
Evasion (level 7). When a spell or trap lets you make a Dexterity save for half damage, you take none on a success and half on a failure.
Shadow-Born (level 9). In dim light or darkness you have advantage on Stealth, and a creature that does not see you does not gain advantage against you.
Thief's Luck (level 10). Once per safe rest, turn a miss into a hit, or a failed check into a 20.

p.i: Paladins have sworn to stand against the dark, and their oath stands with them: it heals by their hands, and burns in their blade.

text.p: Skills. Choose 2: Athletics, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Persuasion, Religion. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Chain hauberk, longsword, shield, two spears, holy symbol, a delver's pack; or (B) 115 gc.

Laying On of Hands (level 1). You have a pool of healing equal to five times your Paladin level, refilled by a safe rest. As an action, touch a creature and give it Health from the pool, or spend 5 to end a disease or poison.
Sense the Unholy (level 1). As an action, you know where undead and fiends are within 60 feet, until the end of your next turn. Once per safe rest, plus your Charisma modifier.
Spellcasting (level 2). From 2nd level you cast paladin spells with Charisma; slots as a half-caster (Kraken counts them).
Smite (level 2). When you hit with a melee weapon, spend a spell slot: 2d8 radiant damage more, +1d8 per circle above the first, +1d8 against undead or fiends.
Oath's Shelter (level 3). You and companions within 10 feet of you cannot be frightened while you are conscious.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Extra Attack (level 5). When you take the Attack action you attack twice.
Aura of Resolve (level 6). You and companions within 10 feet add your Charisma modifier (at least 1) to their saving throws while you are conscious.
Radiant Arms (level 10). Every melee weapon hit you make deals 1d8 radiant damage more.

p.i: Rangers know the wild places between the towns and the ruins, and what hunts there. They track it, and they hunt it back.

tr.td: Light and medium armour and shields

text.p: Skills. Choose 3: Animal Handling, Athletics, Insight, Investigation, Nature, Perception, Stealth, Survival. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Hide coat, two shortswords, longbow and 40 arrows, a delver's pack; or (B) 90 gc.

Pathfinder (level 1). You and companions travelling with you cannot be lost by anything but magic, and you always know which way is north and how far you have come. Foraging finds food for two more people.
Favoured Prey (level 1). Choose beasts, the undead, or the folk of the deep (goblins and their kin): advantage to track them and recall what you know of them, and +2 damage against them.
Spellcasting (level 2). From 2nd level you cast ranger spells with Wisdom; slots as a half-caster.
Fighting Style (level 2). Archer (+2 to ranged attack rolls) or Twin Blades (add your ability modifier to the off-hand attack's damage).
Hunter's Eye (level 3). Once per turn, a weapon hit on a creature you have marked with Hunter's Quarry deals 1d8 more damage.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Extra Attack (level 5). When you take the Attack action you attack twice.
Night Eyes (level 6). You see in dim light as if it were bright, and in darkness 30 feet as if it were dim.
Unseen Hunter (level 10). Hiding is a bonus action for you, and you stay hidden after a missed attack.

p.i: Bards are lorekeepers: they remember the old songs, the names of the dead, and where the stairs go. Their stories keep the dark at bay.

tr.td: Simple weapons, hand crossbows, longswords, rapiers and shortswords

text.p: Skills. Choose any 3. Starting gear. Choose A or B: (A) Leather jerkin, rapier, dagger, a worn instrument (arcane focus), a delver's pack; or (B) 55 gc.
Spellcasting (level 1). You cast bard spells with Charisma: spell save DC 8 + your proficiency + Charisma. You know four spells and learn one more each level.

Inspiration (level 1). Three times per safe rest (more with Charisma: your modifier, at least 3), when a companion who can hear you rolls a d20, add 1d4 to it after seeing the roll but before the outcome is told. The die is 1d6 at 5th level and 1d8 at 9th.
Fireside Tales (level 1). During a safe rest, every companion who listens regains 1 more Health per Recovery Die spent, and loses 1 Dread more.
Jack of All Trades (level 2). Add half your proficiency bonus to checks you are not proficient in.
Expertise (level 3). Choose two skills you are proficient in: double your proficiency bonus for them. Two more at 10th level.
Ability Improvement (level 4). Add 2 to one ability score, or 1 to two (to a most of 20). Again at 8th level.
Song of Courage (level 6). As an action, until the end of your next turn, companions who can hear you have advantage on saves against being frightened and ignore new Dread.
Lore of the Lost (level 10). Learn two spells from any class's list; they are bard spells for you.

Grave Digger (Athletics, Religion). You buried the dead of a town that had too many. You know the old rites, and what a disturbed grave looks like. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Shovel, Holy Symbol, 10 gc; or (B) 20 gc. A shovel, a holy symbol of the dead, 10 gc.

Lamplighter (Perception, Investigation). You kept the street lamps of a city burning through the long nights. You know how long a flame lasts, and what moves when it goes out. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Lantern, Hooded, 2 Oil, Flask, 10 gc; or (B) 20 gc. A hooded lantern, two flasks of oil, 10 gc.
Deserter (Athletics, Stealth). You fled a war you did not believe in, and they are still looking for you. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Dagger, 5 gc; or (B) 10 gc. A worn sword-belt, a forged pass, 5 gc.

Acolyte of the Ash (Religion, Insight). You served a temple that keeps vigil fires against the dark. Its priests will give you a meal and a bed, and ask questions. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Holy Symbol, 10 gc; or (B) 15 gc. A holy symbol, prayer beads, incense, 10 gc.
Smuggler (Deception, Sleight of Hand). You moved what was not allowed across borders that were not watched. You know who to pay, and how much. Gear: 15 gc. A coat with hidden pockets, 15 gc.

Hedge Scholar (Arcana, History). You learned from books nobody else wanted, in libraries nobody else visited. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Ink and Quill, 10 gc; or (B) 15 gc. Ink, a quill, a book of half-remembered lore, 10 gc.

Hunter (Survival, Nature). You fed your family from the forest's edge, and learned which tracks to follow and which to run from. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Hunting Trap, Dagger, 10 gc; or (B) 20 gc. A hunting trap, a skinning knife, 10 gc.

Street Rat (Stealth, Sleight of Hand). You grew up on the streets and the rooftops, fed by quick hands and quicker feet. Gear: Choose A or B: (A) Lucky Charm, 5 gc; or (B) 10 gc. A map of a city's back ways, a lucky charm, 5 gc.

Below ground, time is kept in exploration turns of ten minutes. Each turn the party moves, searches, rests a little, or works at something; the Game Master tracks the turns, and every so often rolls to see whether something finds you.

Nobody sees in total darkness. Elves, half-elves, dwarves and gnomes have Dimsight: in faint light they find their way and see shapes, but cannot read or see detail far off. In darkness they are as blind as anyone.
Light is seen. A lit torch can be seen far further than it lights. In the dark, the creatures that live there see you coming long before you see them.
In Kraken, the map shows light as it falls: carry a torch on your token and your light moves with you. When the light runs out, it is dark.
Every adventurer has a Dread track from 0 to 6. The dark gets into people.

Gaining Dread. The Game Master gives you 1 Dread when your light goes out in a dangerous place, when you see something no one should, when a companion falls, or when magic of fear touches you. Truly horrible things give 2.
Shaken (3 or more). You have disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saves.

Broken (6). Something in you gives way. You choose with the Game Master: you flee, freeze, or fight blindly for a few rounds, and you gain a lasting fear, a nightmare, or a scar. Your Dread then drops to 3.
Losing Dread. A safe rest by a fire lowers Dread by 1. A cleric's Steadying Word, a bard's tales, and some spells lower it more. Some things only time and home can heal.
In Kraken, Dread is the row of six marks on your sheet's main page: click to set it.
A short rest is one exploration turn of quiet. You may spend Recovery Dice (one per level; the die is your class's hit die) and regain the roll plus your Constitution modifier each.

A safe rest is eight hours somewhere safe, with food, water and a bedroll. You regain half your maximum Health (at least 1), half your Recovery Dice, your spell slots and your class's uses, and lose 1 Dread.
Without food, water or safety, a rest does not count as safe.
Initiative. Everyone rolls d20 + Dexterity. Highest first.
Your turn. Move up to your speed and take one action: attack, cast a spell, dash, dodge, help, hide, or use something. Some features give you a bonus action, and you have one reaction a round.

Attacking. Roll d20 + Strength (melee) or Dexterity (ranged or finesse), + your proficiency bonus if you know the weapon, against the target's Defense. A natural 20 is a critical hit: roll the damage dice twice. A natural 1 always misses.
Defense is 10 + Dexterity, or your armour's value (+ Dexterity, as the armour allows), + 2 with a shield.
In Kraken, target a creature (Ctrl+click its token) and use the weapon on your sheet's Combat page or the tracker: the roll, the hit and the damage are worked out for you.
At 0 Health a character is dying: they fall, and cannot act.

At each of their turns a dying character loses 1 Health. An ally beside them may use an action to steady them: a Wisdom check against 12 (a healer's satchel does it without a roll). A steadied character stops bleeding and stays unconscious until healed.
Any healing brings a dying character back from 0.
A character dies when their Health reaches minus their maximum. Monsters die at 0.
In Kraken, a dying character's tracker row has a Steady button: an ally presses it, and their Wisdom is rolled.
Clerics, wizards and bards cast spells from 1st level; paladins and rangers from 2nd. Spells come in circles (1st to 3rd in this book) and cantrips, which cost nothing.
Casting a spell of a circle uses a slot of that circle or higher; slots return after a safe rest. A spell cast in a higher slot is often stronger.
Your spell save DC is 8 + your proficiency + your casting ability; your spell attack is your proficiency + your casting ability.
Magic does not light the dark unless it says so, and it is noticed: the Game Master may roll for wandering things after loud or bright magic.
Descending Darkness is an original game made for Kraken VTT. Its text and setting are original, and it may be shared freely with Kraken.

Its game mechanics are in the family of the world's most played fantasy roleplaying game.
